rounds.text: Bajaj Auto Ltd is demonstrating exceptional fundamental momentum, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 37% [E17] and a compounded profit growth of 55% [E21]. This robust operational performance is underpinned by elite capital efficiency, featuring a return on equity of 29.2% [E13] and an ROCE of 28.2% [E12], both vastly superior to sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Far from cooling off, the business is constrained only by a high-class problem: surging demand has hit capacity limits, prompting an ambitious 25% plant expansion from 7 million to 9 million units per annum to unlock growth in EVs, high-end motorcycles, and three-wheelers [E84, E85, E90]. Crucially, a discounted cash flow model suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 15,936 per share, establishing a tangible margin of safety of 26.2% against the current market price [E46, E47]. Conceded: the stock trades at a rich price-to-book ratio of 8.47x [E2] and faces near-term margin friction from a 4.5% revenue impact due to accelerated metal inflation [E88]. However, management successfully expanded EBITDA margins sequentially to 20.9% despite this hyperinflationary commodity environment [E89], proving their unmatched pricing power and operational fortitude.

Bajaj Auto carries significant valuation and structural risks that the underlying evidence does not adequately support at the current market price. The stock trades at an expensive P/E of 27.4x to 28.06x [E1, E6] and commands a lofty price-to-book multiple of 8.35x to 8.47x [E2, E7], sitting well above sector benchmarks. Furthermore, institutional money flow is negative with foreign institutions cutting their stake from 14.37% down to 9.01% [E43, E45], signaling a lack of confidence from sophisticated market participants. Conceded: the company displays strong historical return metrics such as an ROE of 29.2% and robust 5-year and 3-year compounded profit growth [E13, E19, E20]. However, earnings growth is actively decelerating according to the rules-based screen [E69], while borrowings have surged sharply to Rs 22,713 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 9,364 Cr a year prior [E40]. Operational efficiency is also questionable as cash conversion sits at a weak 0.25x with operating cash flow making up only 46% of operating profit [E34, E37], while recent supply chain issues, raw material inflation, and a ransomware attack caused a 10% to 15% impairment in availabilities [E96, E97].

Conceded: the stock trades above sector P/B benchmarks at 8.35x to 8.47x [E2, E7]. However, this premium valuation is fully justified by world-class profitability metrics that dwarf the broader sector, specifically an ROE of 27.67% versus the sector's 11.39% and an ROCE of 24.52% against a sector benchmark of 12.54% [E9, E10]. While foreign institutions reduced their holdings, domestic institutions aggressively stepped up their stake from 9.03% to 13.42%, demonstrating robust local conviction [E44]. The surge in borrowings to Rs 22,713 Cr [E40] directly funds a massive 2393.4% jump in capital work-in-progress [E41] and a 25% capacity expansion toward 9 million units [E84], proving the debt is productive growth capital rather than structural distress. Conceded: cash conversion dipped to 0.25x for Mar 2026 [E34], but the company generated over INR 2,300 crores of free cash flow in Q1 alone—nearly doubling year-on-year—with cash conversion reaching 80% of profit after tax [E93]. Finally, the operational headwinds from supply chain disruptions and the ransomware attack [E96] were successfully defended while the company still delivered record financial performance [E98] and a high rules-based screen score of 86 out of 100 [E64].

Conceded: the company posted high ROE and ROCE metrics that outpace sector benchmarks [E9, E10], and domestic institutions increased their stake [E44]. However, citing these strengths ignores the severe reality of institutional money flow reading negative alongside a 5.36 percentage point exodus by foreign institutional investors [E43, E45]. Conceded: the company expanded capacity and generated free cash flow in Q1 [E84, E93], but this does not erase the alarming surge in borrowings to ₹ 22,713 Cr [E40] and the drop in full-year cash conversion to a dismal 0.25x where profits completely outstripped actual operating cash [E34]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes operational friction by dismissing the ransomware attack, supply chain breakdowns, and logistics failures that impaired availabilities by up to 15% and erased 10% of production volume [E96, E97, E98]. Finally, a rules-based screen score [E64] cannot override the explicit warning signals of decelerating earnings growth, negative institutional money flow, and an expensive valuation trading at over 8 times book value [E63, E69, E70].

Conceded: foreign institutional investors reduced their holdings by 5.36 percentage points [E43], and cash conversion for the full year touched 0.25x [E34]. However, the bear's focus on short-term production volume losses ignores that capacities have emerged as the primary constraint to growth [E90], proving that unfulfilled demand is the core operational bottleneck rather than structural weakness. Conceded: borrowings rose to ₹ 22,713 Cr [E40], but this is explicitly tied to a massive 2,393.4% surge in capital work-in-progress [E41] and a 25% capacity expansion toward 9 million units [E84], representing high-conviction growth spending. The disruptions from the ransomware attack and supply chain issues were defended comprehensively and successfully, allowing the business to still deliver record volumes and financial performance [E98]. Furthermore, domestic institutions absorbed the institutional shift by increasing their stake by 4.39 percentage points [E44], and a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 15,936 per share, leaving a clear margin of safety of 26.2% [E46, E47].

Conceded: capacities have emerged as a key constraint to growth [E90]. However, framing production constraints as merely an unfulfilled demand bottleneck ignores that these same disruptions impaired availabilities by 10% to 15% and caused a direct loss of production opportunities amounting to 10% of volume during the quarter [E97, E98]. Conceded: capital work-in-progress surged by 2,393.4% [E41], but this aggressive capex build-up has ballooned borrowings to ₹ 22,713 Cr—a severe escalation from ₹ 9,364 Cr a year earlier [E40]. While domestic institutions increased their stake by 4.39 percentage points [E44], this has not offset broader institutional flight, as evidenced by foreign institutions slashing holdings by 5.36 percentage points [E43] and scanX flagging negative institutional money flow [E45]. Finally, relying on a discounted cash flow valuation to claim a margin of safety [E46, E47] disregards explicit internal warnings that the rich valuation at a P/E of 27.4 and P/B of 8.47 already discounts the good news [E1, E2, E71].
